A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LFP task and LFPBench research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original LLM evaluations on LFPBench, including judgment accuracy, model screening, and analyses of evidence-order and evidence-quantity biases.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds human evaluation, direct fact-quality scores, F1 results, and a rewritten-fact experiment.

M1.justification: The proposed evidence-to-facts-to-judgment pipeline, task mappings, and five prompt templates remain unchanged. DP-Prompt rewriting is introduced for an evaluation experiment, without changing the proposed prediction procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 657 Chinese cases covering ten civil case types. v3 adds a limited input-quality scenario by evaluating four rewritten fact variants with differing similarities. The human evaluation samples existing coverage; the datasets described in new Table 1 are not additionally evaluated.

E2.justification: The main six-model, three-pipeline comparison and legal-model screening retain their participants. The corresponding Figure 5 analysis now includes only four general-purpose models, omitting Law-Llama3.1-8B and LawJustice-Llama3.1-8B, which appeared in v2.

E3.justification: v3 adds an evaluation by two legal experts on 100 randomly selected cases containing 259 claims, ROUGE and ten-point GPT-4o judging, and macro/micro-F1. It replaces cross-model correlations using ChatLaw/OpenAI embeddings with evaluation of four Qwen2.5-14B/DP-Prompt fact rewrites. These substantially extend evaluation procedures without establishing changes to the retained main experiments.

E4.justification: New Section 3.3 tests whether extracted evidence supports accurate human judgments, addressing dataset usability. Finding 3 replaces the cross-model correlation with a within-model fact-quality sensitivity experiment. These materially expand validation and analysis; the existing case-type, outcome, evidence-order, and evidence-quantity analyses remain.

E5.justification: v3 Finding 3 newly reports three repetitions per parameter setting for the rewritten-fact experiment. v2 gives no corresponding run count. No seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added, and the disclosure does not establish an increase in runs for retained experiments.

E6.justification: The retained accuracy and screening tables are numerically unchanged. v3 adds expert results, ROUGE/LLM-judge scores, macro/micro-F1, and rewritten-fact curves replacing the original correlations. For example, Table 5 reports a 6.23 judge score for Llama3.1-Chinese-8B. The new human accuracy is internally inconsistent: Table 3 gives 87.62%, while Section 3.3 gives 87.26%.

T1.justification: The formal definitions involving C, Z, f(C,Z), and g(C,f(C,Z)) are retained. The added arithmetic explaining the existing 7.42% accuracy decrease and the prose definition of evidence introduce no new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: introducing LFP, constructing the first LFP benchmark, and demonstrating its usefulness for LJP. The claimed 38.5% average reduction in the evidence-based performance gap and the principal model limitations remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 newly interprets human performance as evidence that extraction preserves most critical information and defends the single-jurisdiction scope. Ethical Considerations replaces the generic bias/auditing discussion with an untested argument that LFP can reduce judicial bias and clarifies its assistance role. The trial-stage applicability discussion moves unchanged to Appendix A.

D1.justification: The code/data destination changes from HPRCEST/LFPBench to teijyogen/LFP, and the GPT-4o-0513 snapshot identifier is shortened to GPT-4o. Dataset construction newly specifies expert selection of moderately difficult case types and consistency review. Existing model documentation, hyperparameters, and prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: New Table 1 expands benchmark positioning, including SwissJP, Auto-Judge, BrCase, and PhilCases. v3 adds references for the LJP survey, ROUGE, and DP-Prompt, and replaces Korn with Wex definitions. The central relationship to fact-based LJP and legal document summarization remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 moves the main Discussion to Appendix A, adds human-evaluation and F1 subsections, and locally revises background, dataset, and ethics prose. Author affiliations, contribution notes, acknowledgments, and the conference header also change. Most existing narrative and section progression are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds benchmark-comparison, human-evaluation, direct-LFP-score, and F1 tables. Figure 5 changes from two scatterplots to a four-series line chart, while Figure 6 becomes more compact with a shared legend. These substantially revise the visual presentation, alongside relocation of existing figures, tables, and appendix prompts.

improvement.justification: Human validation addresses v2's concern about information lost during evidence extraction, and the within-model rewriting experiment improves on its cross-model correlation. Direct fact-quality and macro-F1 reporting also broaden assessment. These provide a limited net gain, constrained by conflicting human accuracy figures, unexplained micro-F1/accuracy mismatches, and the new untested judicial-bias reduction argument.
